# Reduced Motion

<!-- Generated by generate-swiftui-skill.py; edit the library sources. -->

Category: Accessibility

Toggle the simulated reduced-motion preference to compare unconditional movement with an immediate state update; both panels always respect the actual system accessibility setting.

- Before: Simulated preference is ignored
- After: Motion adapts to the preference

APIs: `accessibilityReduceMotion`, `animation`

## Complete improved example

Adapt the behavior to the app; demonstration controls and values are illustrative.

```swift
import SwiftUI

// iOS 17+. Present ReducedDoExample() in your app.
struct ReducedDoExample: View {
    @State private var phase = 0
    @State private var resetID = 0
    @State private var simulated = true
    var body: some View {
        VStack(spacing: 20) {
            ReducedDoContent(phase: phase, simulateReducedMotion: simulated)
                .frame(maxWidth: 320, minHeight: 180)
                .id(resetID)
            Button("Run example") { phase += 1 }
            Toggle("Simulate Reduce Motion", isOn: $simulated)
            Button("Reset") { phase = 0; simulated = true; resetID += 1 }
        }
        .padding()
    }
}

struct ReducedDoContent: View {
    let phase: Int
    @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) private var reduceMotion
    var simulateReducedMotion = true

    var body: some View {
        // excerpt:start
        Label(phase.isMultiple(of: 2) ? "Photo 1" : "Photo 2", systemImage: "photo")
            .offset(x: (reduceMotion || simulateReducedMotion) ? 0 : (phase.isMultiple(of: 2) ? -40 : 40))
            .animation((reduceMotion || simulateReducedMotion) ? nil : .smooth, value: phase)
        // Both examples always honor the actual system preference.
        // excerpt:end
    }

}
```
